title: Austin's Big Dam Project, Oil Tanks, & Street Upgrades
summary:
*   **Austin's critical dam rebuilding project advanced:** The city authorized a surveyor to map land to be flooded by the new dam and extended the contractors' timeline due to flood delays, acknowledging over $58,000 spent on the project.
*   **Major infrastructure upgrades approved:** The council appropriated $4,500 to purchase land for new City Stables and established permanent street grades for a section of Lavacca Street.
*   **First petroleum storage permit issued:** A permit was granted to the Pierce-Fordyce Oil Association for an underground 300-gallon gasoline tank and pump on West 6th Street, requiring strict engineering and fire marshal oversight.
*   **Cemetery plot modified for monument:** A crosswalk in Oakwood Cemetery was vacated for Dr. and Mrs. Maxwell to erect a monument, provided they construct a new public cement walkway.

Resolved that the Supt of Parks and Public Property be authorized to employ O E Metcalf at
a compensation of $6.00 per day and necessary expenses, to survey survey the land that
will be overflowed by the Colorado River on account of the dam now being re-built across
said River.
The resolution was adopted by a vote of 4 Ayes, Councilman Bartholomew not voting The
Mayor laid before the Council the following resolution: Whereas, it appears from
satisfactory evidence to us in the original receipts of the Wm P Carmichael Co, verified
by the City Auditor, Milton Morris, and from the certificate of the Inspector at the dam,
Mr S Ponder , that the City Dam Contractors
time extended
Water Power Co, did, in the period between Oct 14th 1912, and Dec 28th 1912, expend in the
work of re-building the Austin Dam the sum of $58,073.61, and are entitled to sixteen (16)
days time for time lost by floods and other causes not within the control of said City
Water Power Co; Therefore; Be it resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin : That
the City Water Power Co, Contractors, assignees of Wm D Johnson ,have to date complied
with the conditions of their franchise to rebuild the dam, and that the sixth period of
the franchise under said contract begins on December 28th, 1912, and that said City Water
Power Co has expended more than the required amount of money in the fifth period of their
contract required by the terms of their contract .
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Bartholomew, Hart, Haynes & R W owell 5 Nays none.
Approved, A P Wooldridge, Mayor.
The Council then recessed subject to call.

Austin, Texas.

I want permission to tack up a piece of canvas in front of my store 200 East 6th street,

Tuesday January 21st 1913.
The Council was called to order by the Mayor with all members present: The Mayor laid
before the Council the following resolution : Be it resolved by the City Council of the
City of Austin : That permit be and is hereby granted the Pierce-Fordyce Oil Association
to install and maintain in the alley in the rear of No 203 West 6th street a gasoline tank
,for the purpose of storing gasoline.Said tank is to be undergroundBowser tank of 300
gallons capacity.

Pierce Fordyce Oil
Co. Permit

It must not be placed less than two feet under ground,and installed under the supervision
jointly of the City Engineer and Fire Marshal of this City.
Authority is also granted to said Pierce-Fordyce Oil Association to instal a gasoline pump
,to be used in connection with said Gasoline tank,within the premises occupied by said
Pierce-Fordyce Oil Association,at 203 West 6th street.
This permit is granted and is to be received and accepted as being revocable at the

hereby vacated and authorized by the Council to be closed.
Vacation
Cemetary Lot

Be it further resolved:
That the owners of said lots be and they are hereby authorized to erect a monument in or
